newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo Wellcome down on NovoPharm deal.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo Wellcome down on NovoPharm deal.

text.p: Shares in British drugs company Glaxo Wellcome Plc gave up modest gains to trade lower after the company said on Thursday it would not pursue an appeal of patent infringement litigation against NovoPharm Biotech Inc, dealers said.
Glaxo shares were down 12 pence, or 1.03 percent, to 1,153.5pp by 1100 GMT while the FTSE-100 index was unchanged at 4,387.7. Glaxo hit a 1,177p high earlier.
Glaxo said in a statement that its U.S. unit Glaxo Wellcome Inc had signed a licensing agreement allowing NovoPharm Inc to market a generic form of Glaxo's ulcer treatment Zantac.
Under the deal, Novopharm will be able to market its generic treatment 16 days earlier than other manufacturers, a Glaxo spokesman said. In return, Glaxo will receive payments from Novopharm.
The U.S. Court of Appeals recently ruled NovoPharm could produce a generic drug of Glaxo's ulcer drug Zantac.
